notes: GATE P2 REGRESSION RERUN, clean tree. Rebuilt from scratch after four runtime-hardening changes: the full-download path moved into a per-transaction workspace (blocker B4), every stage of the tar pipeline gained a local size ceiling, BlobStore::put stopped inferring a stored blob from an occupied path, and abandoned transaction workspaces became collectable. WHAT THIS IS EVIDENCE FOR: that the hardening did not close the fast path it protects. It is NOT independent evidence for the guards themselves -- those are proven by unit and flow tests plus five mutations, because a happy-path E2E cannot exercise a cap that is never approached or a race that does not occur. WHY THE AUTHENTICATED PATH IS PROVEN TO HAVE RUN, unchanged from the Gate P1 rerun: a signature with no delta-v1 binding parses as Legacy, and a Legacy binding makes both delta paths unavailable by construction, so a tar-delta outcome is unreachable without a parsed, verified, matching identity. Transition 2 installed from a tar delta. One decoded comment, from manifest-1.0.2.json: 'delta-v1 app:dev.chahdane.delta-updater-example v:1.0.2 plat:darwin-aarch64 rep:app-tar-gz-v1 b3:a8c1cd78be6f08c5d392a5566244c6948bdda94ab5b9e1d3b8509aab577d5a58 sz:4177582 ts:1786668567'. The three main binaries hash to b96b8ffb..., bb7609f5... and a85548e9... (SHA-256) and are asserted pairwise distinct. Transition 1 is a full download because the cache starts empty -- cold-start behaviour, not a fallback. The degradation case corrupts the cached base blob and confirms the update still completes via a full download rather than a tar delta. CONFOUNDER, stated again: the only source difference between versions is a version string, so 15.3% is a best case for this shape of change and not a general expectation. The ratios reproduce the Gate P1 run (15.0% and 15.4%) on independently rebuilt artifacts.
artifact_provenance: examples/desktop-app/e2e/build-three-versions.sh /private/tmp/delta-p2-e2e, which runs `cargo tauri build --features e2e-control` three times against examples/desktop-app with only the version string changed, then publishes both releases with the delta-release binary built from this tree, passing --app-id derived from tauri.conf.json's identifier and --require-tar-layer. Replayed by examples/desktop-app/e2e/run-tar-e2e.sh against a local HTTP server; the app under test is the real bundled .app, launched and relaunched between transitions so promotion is licensed by what actually ran. The build script rewrites the example's version, signing key and plain-HTTP opt-in in place; those edits are per-run scratch and were reverted before commit.
